name: Ligustrazine (tetramethylpyrazine)
short: Stroke trial reviews: only 10 of 19 and 1 of 3 trials assessed safety; those found no obvious side effects. Low-quality trials. Lung fibrosis review: adverse reactions not significantly different.
text: The human data come from meta-analyses of randomised trials, and the cited abstracts do not state how ligustrazine was given (by mouth or by injection). In a meta-analysis of 19 trials (1969 patients) of ligustrazine in cerebral infarction, only ten trials contained safety assessments, and they stated that no obvious side effects were found; the authors described the research as low quality. In a meta-analysis of three trials (643 patients) of ligustrazine added to conventional medicine in ischaemic stroke, only one trial assessed safety, and no adverse events were reported; the methodological quality of all three was generally poor. In a meta-analysis of 7 trials (366 patients) in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, the abstract reports the comparison of adverse reactions between groups as not significant (P = 0.45), and the authors said that the safety and adverse reactions of ligustrazine need further analysis. No case reports were found in the searches, and no interaction data were found in the cited sources.
